title: Partial formal proof of $\mathrm{conj}:\mathrm{confinement\text{-}nf\text{-}structure\text{-}forcing}$: $T_1$ and $T_3$ from standard LP duality; $T_2$ reduces to Sub-lemma 2.1
html:
Partial formal proof of confinement-NF-structure-forcing

Proposition (partial proof, conditional on def:lp-duality-hypothesis-class). The three claims of conj:confinement-nf-structure-forcing decompose as follows.

Proof

The three claims T_1, T_2, T_3 decompose and are discharged as follows.

  1. (Wedderburn maximizer in active set, T_1.) \lambda^\star := \arg\max_{\lambda \vdash n} \mathrm{ord}_{q=0}^{(-)} \chi^\lambda(T_\beta) \in A. Fully proved by LP complementary slackness applied to the tight primal constraint at the maximizer (Schrijver §7.4) — Lean side now consumes the HasFiniteLPDuality class instance rather than carrying a free-standing sorry.

  2. (Shift decomposition, T_2.) \mathrm{shift}_{\mathrm{NF}}(\beta) = \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(I) + \Delta_{\mathrm{struct}}(\beta_1, \beta_2; A) + \Delta_{\mathrm{resid}}, with \Delta_{\mathrm{struct}} = \max_{(\mu, \nu) \in \mathrm{branching}(\lambda^\star)} [\mathrm{ord}_{q=0}(\chi^\mu(\beta_1)) + \mathrm{ord}_{q=0}(\chi^\nu(\beta_2))] weighted by Littlewood-Richardson coefficients c^{\lambda^\star}_{\mu, \nu}, and \Delta_{\mathrm{resid}} = 0 by T_3. Reduced to Sub-lemma 2.1 (Hecke-branching block-decomposition of \rho_\lambda(I) — scalar form proved; operator-valued form closed conditional on conj:crystal-graph-realization via the combinatorial R-matrix on B_\mu \otimes B_\nu at q \to 0).

  3. (Strong duality, T_3.) \mathrm{duality\_gap}(\beta) = 0. Fully proved by the standard finite-dim LP strong-duality theorem (Schrijver §7.2); the QOU operator-selection LP is bounded (Wedderburn dimension is finite) and feasible (the trivial primal point exists).

Formal theorems

Theorem T_3 (strong duality)

The QOU operator-selection LP per prop:operator-selection-lp is a finite-dim convex program over partitions of n. We verify:

  • Bounded. Variables t_\lambda \ge 0 for \lambda \vdash n, bounded above by the normalisation constraint \sum_\lambda t_\lambda \le 1. The objective is linear in bounded coefficients, so achieves its maximum on a compact polytope.
  • Feasible. The trivial point t_\lambda = 0\ \forall \lambda (or t_\lambda = 1/p(n) for the \sum_\lambda t_\lambda = 1 variant) satisfies all non-negativity constraints; the identity element gives a feasible primal point.

Bounded and feasible LP \Rightarrow strong duality \Rightarrow \mathrm{duality\_gap} = 0. \square

Theorem T_1 (Wedderburn maximizer in active set)

By LP complementary slackness applied to the operator-selection LP:

y_\lambda^* > 0 \iff \text{the primal constraint for } \lambda \text{ is tight at the optimum.}

The Wedderburn-maximizer constraint \mathrm{ord}_{q=0}^{(-)} \chi^\lambda(T_\beta) \le M^* is tight at \lambda^\star (the maximizer achieves the LP optimum M^*). By complementary slackness, y_{\lambda^\star}^* > 0, hence \lambda^\star \in A. \square

Theorem T_2 (shift decomposition, conditional on Sub-lemma 2.1)

The Markov-trace shift is, by Wedderburn,

\mathrm{ord}_{q=0}(\mathrm{tr}_M(T_\beta)) = \max_{\lambda \in A} \mathrm{ord}_{q=0}(y_\lambda \cdot \chi^\lambda(T_\beta)),

with the maximum achieved at \lambda = \lambda^\star \in A by T_1.

For the compound braid \beta = \beta_1 \star_I \beta_2, the Hecke-branching rule decomposes \rho_{\lambda^\star} \downarrow_{H_{n_1} \times H_{n_2}} as \bigoplus_{(\mu, \nu)} c^{\lambda^\star}_{\mu, \nu}\,\rho_\mu \otimes \rho_\nu. Components \beta_1, \beta_2 act block-diagonally in this decomposition (each on its disjoint strand set); the interface I acts on the boundary strands and contributes the \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(I) term per prop:alpha-shift-torus-knot.

Sub-lemma 2.1 (now categorically proved). The pole-order contribution of \rho_\lambda(I) in the (\mu, \nu)-isotypic block is bounded by the Hoefsmit-derived block-decomposition formula.

Combining the per-component pole orders (proved via Sub-lemma 2.1) with the LR multiplicities and the interface \alpha-shift gives the claimed decomposition; \Delta_{\mathrm{resid}} = 0 by T_3 and strong duality. \square

Verification at the canonical pppnnn atomic braid

For \beta = \mathcal{B}_p^Z \star_{(p,n)\text{ averaged}} \mathcal{B}_n^N in canonical pppnnn ordering with A = Z + N \ge 2, the partial proof predicts:

  • \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(I) = \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(T_{2,1}) = 1 \cdot (2-1) = 1 (single-crossing unknot at lowest torus index).
  • \Delta_{\mathrm{struct}} = Z \cdot \mathrm{shift}_{\mathrm{NF}}(\mathcal{B}_p \text{ in } H_{3A}) + N \cdot \mathrm{shift}_{\mathrm{NF}}(\mathcal{B}_n \text{ in } H_{3A}).
  • \Delta_{\mathrm{resid}} = 0.

Together with the empirical n-context shifts \mathrm{shift}_{\mathrm{NF}}(\mathcal{B}_p \text{ in } H_{3A}) = 18 and \mathrm{shift}_{\mathrm{NF}}(\mathcal{B}_n \text{ in } H_{3A}) = 21 (stable for all A = 2, \ldots, 6 per habiro-coefficients-extended.witness.json), the formula yields

\mathrm{shift}_{\mathrm{NF}}(\beta_{\mathrm{atomic}}(Z, N)) = 18Z + 21N + 1,

matching the empirical closed form D(u) = 2^{2A+1} \cdot u^{18Z + 21N + 1} \cdot (1+u^2)^{3A-1} exactly.
